about: Labelled flashcards for the card-quality benchmark (scripts/bench/cards.mjs). Notes and cards written for Gradify. Each card is 'good' or has one known defect. Defects: leak (the question gives the answer away), vague (no clear subject), yes-no, ungrounded (the quote isn't in the notes), wrong (the answer contradicts the notes), unsupported (the answer adds claims the notes don't make), duplicate (repeats an earlier card), multi (tests two unrelated things), ambiguous (more than one answer could fairly be right), trivial (not worth learning). A good card's quote appears in its notes.

sets.subject: chemistry
sets.notes: SN2 reactions happen in a single concerted step: the nucleophile attacks the carbon from the side opposite the leaving group, so the configuration at that carbon is inverted (Walden inversion). The rate depends on both the substrate and the nucleophile, so rate = k[RX][Nu-]. SN2 is fastest for methyl and primary haloalkanes, because bulky groups block the backside attack. SN1 reactions go through a carbocation intermediate; the rate-determining step is loss of the leaving group, so rate = k[RX]. Tertiary haloalkanes favour SN1 because tertiary carbocations are stabilised by the inductive effect of the alkyl groups. Polar protic solvents such as water stabilise the carbocation and favour SN1.

cards.front: What is the rate equation for an SN2 reaction?
cards.quote: so rate = k[RX][Nu-]
cards.label: good

cards.front: Why are tertiary haloalkanes slow to react by SN2?
cards.back: Bulky groups block the nucleophile's backside attack on the carbon.
cards.quote: because bulky groups block the backside attack
cards.label: good

cards.front: What happens to the configuration at the carbon in an SN2 reaction?
cards.quote: the configuration at that carbon is inverted (Walden inversion)
cards.label: good

cards.front: What is the rate-determining step of an SN1 reaction?
cards.back: Attack of the nucleophile on the carbocation.
cards.quote: the rate-determining step is loss of the leaving group
cards.label: wrong

cards.front: What is the rate equation of an SN1 reaction, where rate = k[RX]?
cards.quote: so rate = k[RX]
cards.label: leak

cards.front: Which solvents favour SN2 reactions?
cards.back: Polar aprotic solvents such as acetone and DMSO.
cards.quote: Polar aprotic solvents such as acetone favour SN2
cards.label: ungrounded

sets.subject: biology
sets.notes: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm and splits one glucose molecule into two molecules of pyruvate. It produces a net gain of two ATP and two reduced NAD per glucose. In aerobic conditions pyruvate enters the mitochondrial matrix and is converted to acetyl coenzyme A in the link reaction, releasing carbon dioxide. The Krebs cycle also takes place in the mitochondrial matrix. Oxidative phosphorylation happens on the inner mitochondrial membrane, where the electron transport chain pumps protons into the intermembrane space; ATP synthase uses the proton gradient to make ATP. Oxygen is the final electron acceptor and is reduced to water.

cards.front: Where in the cell does glycolysis take place?
cards.quote: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm
cards.label: good

cards.front: What is the final electron acceptor in oxidative phosphorylation?
cards.back: Oxygen, which is reduced to water
cards.quote: Oxygen is the final electron acceptor and is reduced to water
cards.label: good

cards.front: Glycolysis gives a net gain of _____ ATP per glucose.
cards.quote: It produces a net gain of two ATP and two reduced NAD per glucose
cards.label: good

cards.front: Where in the cell does the process of glycolysis happen?
cards.quote: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm
cards.label: duplicate

cards.front: Where does the Krebs cycle take place, and what does ATP synthase use to make ATP?
cards.back: The mitochondrial matrix; the proton gradient across the inner membrane.
cards.quote: The Krebs cycle also takes place in the mitochondrial matrix
cards.label: multi

cards.front: It happens on the inner mitochondrial membrane. What is it?
cards.quote: Oxidative phosphorylation happens on the inner mitochondrial membrane
cards.label: vague

sets.subject: medicine
sets.notes: Cardiac output is the volume of blood pumped by each ventricle per minute, and equals heart rate multiplied by stroke volume. Stroke volume is end-diastolic volume minus end-systolic volume. The Frank-Starling mechanism means that a greater end-diastolic volume stretches the ventricular muscle and increases the force of contraction, so stroke volume rises. Sympathetic stimulation increases both heart rate and contractility. In hypovolaemic shock, low circulating volume reduces end-diastolic volume, so stroke volume and cardiac output fall; the heart rate rises to compensate. Beta blockers reduce heart rate and contractility.

cards.front: How is stroke volume calculated?
cards.quote: Stroke volume is end-diastolic volume minus end-systolic volume
cards.label: good

cards.front: Why does cardiac output fall in hypovolaemic shock?
cards.back: Low circulating volume reduces end-diastolic volume, so stroke volume falls.
cards.quote: low circulating volume reduces end-diastolic volume, so stroke volume and cardiac output fall
cards.label: good

cards.front: What does the Frank-Starling mechanism describe?
cards.back: A greater end-diastolic volume stretches the ventricle and increases the force of contraction, so stroke volume rises.
cards.quote: a greater end-diastolic volume stretches the ventricular muscle and increases the force of contraction
cards.label: good

cards.front: What effect do beta blockers have on the heart?
cards.back: They increase heart rate and contractility.
cards.quote: Beta blockers reduce heart rate and contractility
cards.label: wrong

cards.front: Is cardiac output heart rate multiplied by stroke volume?
cards.quote: equals heart rate multiplied by stroke volume
cards.label: yes-no

cards.front: What is the normal resting cardiac output of an adult?
cards.quote: a normal resting cardiac output is about 5 litres per minute
cards.label: ungrounded

sets.subject: mathematics
sets.notes: The derivative of x^n is n x^(n-1) for any real n. The chain rule says that if y = f(g(x)) then dy/dx = f'(g(x)) g'(x). The product rule says that the derivative of u v is u' v + u v'. A stationary point is where the first derivative is zero. If the second derivative is positive there, the point is a local minimum; if it is negative, a local maximum; if it is zero, the test is inconclusive. The integral of 1/x is ln|x| + C.

cards.front: What does the chain rule give for dy/dx when y = f(g(x))?
cards.quote: then dy/dx = f'(g(x)) g'(x)
cards.label: good

cards.front: What is the integral of 1/x?
cards.quote: The integral of 1/x is ln|x| + C
cards.label: good

cards.front: At a stationary point the second derivative is zero. What can you conclude?
cards.back: Nothing yet: the second-derivative test is inconclusive.
cards.quote: if it is zero, the test is inconclusive
cards.label: good

cards.front: What is the derivative of u v?
cards.quote: the derivative of u v is u' v + u v'
cards.label: wrong

cards.front: What is a stationary point?
cards.quote: A stationary point is where the first derivative is zero
cards.label: ambiguous

cards.front: What letter is used for the constant of integration?
cards.quote: The integral of 1/x is ln|x| + C
cards.label: trivial

sets.subject: physics
sets.notes: Newton's second law states that the resultant force on a body equals the rate of change of its momentum; for constant mass, F = ma. Momentum is mass multiplied by velocity and is measured in kg m/s. In any collision with no external force, total momentum is conserved. In an elastic collision kinetic energy is also conserved; in an inelastic collision some kinetic energy is transferred to other stores such as heat and sound. Power is the rate of doing work, P = W/t, measured in watts.

cards.back: The resultant force on a body equals its rate of change of momentum.
cards.quote: the resultant force on a body equals the rate of change of its momentum
cards.label: good

cards.front: How does an elastic collision differ from an inelastic one?
cards.back: In an elastic collision kinetic energy is conserved; in an inelastic collision some is transferred to other stores.
cards.quote: In an elastic collision kinetic energy is also conserved
cards.label: good

cards.quote: is measured in kg m/s
cards.label: good

cards.label: leak

cards.quote: In any collision with no external force, total momentum is conserved
cards.label: wrong

cards.back: The rate of change of its momentum
cards.quote: the resultant force on a body equals the rate of change of its momentum
cards.label: duplicate

sets.subject: computer science
sets.notes: Binary search finds an item in a sorted list by repeatedly halving the search interval, so it takes O(log n) comparisons in the worst case. It only works if the list is sorted. Merge sort divides the list in half, sorts each half recursively and merges them; it runs in O(n log n) time in every case and needs O(n) extra space. Quicksort is O(n log n) on average but O(n^2) in the worst case, which happens when the pivot is repeatedly the smallest or largest item. A hash table gives average O(1) lookup.

cards.quote: so it takes O(log n) comparisons in the worst case
cards.label: good

cards.front: When does quicksort take O(n^2) time?
cards.back: When the pivot is repeatedly the smallest or largest item.
cards.quote: which happens when the pivot is repeatedly the smallest or largest item
cards.label: good

cards.front: What extra space does merge sort need?
cards.quote: needs O(n) extra space
cards.label: good

cards.front: What is the worst-case time complexity of merge sort?
cards.quote: it runs in O(n log n) time in every case
cards.label: wrong

cards.front: What does a hash table give?
cards.quote: A hash table gives average O(1) lookup
cards.label: ambiguous

cards.front: Which is the best sorting algorithm?
cards.back: Merge sort, because it is always O(n log n) and stable.
cards.quote: it runs in O(n log n) time in every case
cards.label: unsupported

sets.subject: law
sets.notes: A contract needs offer, acceptance, consideration and an intention to create legal relations. An invitation to treat, such as goods displayed in a shop window, is not an offer: it invites customers to make offers. Acceptance must be communicated to the offeror, but under the postal rule an acceptance sent by post takes effect when it is posted. Consideration must be sufficient but need not be adequate. Past consideration is generally not good consideration. In domestic and social agreements there is a rebuttable presumption that the parties do not intend to create legal relations.

cards.front: When does a postal acceptance take effect under the postal rule?
cards.quote: an acceptance sent by post takes effect when it is posted
cards.label: good

cards.front: Goods displayed in a shop window are an offer. What's wrong with that?
cards.back: They are an invitation to treat: the customer makes the offer.
cards.quote: An invitation to treat, such as goods displayed in a shop window, is not an offer
cards.label: good

cards.front: What presumption applies to domestic and social agreements?
cards.back: A rebuttable presumption that the parties do not intend to create legal relations
cards.quote: there is a rebuttable presumption that the parties do not intend to create legal relations
cards.label: good

cards.front: Must consideration be adequate?
cards.quote: Consideration must be sufficient but need not be adequate
cards.label: yes-no

cards.front: Which case established the postal rule?
cards.quote: the postal rule was established in Adams v Lindsell
cards.label: ungrounded

cards.front: What does a contract need?
cards.quote: A contract needs offer, acceptance, consideration and an intention to create legal relations
cards.label: ambiguous

sets.subject: psychology
sets.notes: The multi-store model of memory has three stores: sensory register, short-term memory and long-term memory. Short-term memory has a capacity of about seven items, plus or minus two, and a duration of about 18 to 30 seconds without rehearsal. Information moves from short-term to long-term memory through rehearsal. The working memory model replaced the single short-term store with a central executive, a phonological loop, a visuospatial sketchpad and an episodic buffer. Proactive interference is when old learning disrupts new learning; retroactive interference is when new learning disrupts old learning.

cards.back: About seven items, plus or minus two
cards.quote: Short-term memory has a capacity of about seven items, plus or minus two
cards.label: good

cards.front: How does proactive interference differ from retroactive interference?
cards.back: Proactive: old learning disrupts new learning. Retroactive: new learning disrupts old learning.
cards.quote: Proactive interference is when old learning disrupts new learning
cards.label: good

cards.front: How does information move from short-term to long-term memory?
cards.quote: Information moves from short-term to long-term memory through rehearsal
cards.label: good

cards.front: What is retroactive interference?
cards.back: When old learning disrupts new learning
cards.quote: retroactive interference is when new learning disrupts old learning
cards.label: wrong

cards.front: They replaced the single short-term store. What are they?
cards.back: Central executive, phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad and episodic buffer
cards.quote: a central executive, a phonological loop, a visuospatial sketchpad and an episodic buffer
cards.label: vague

cards.front: Who proposed the working memory model, and in what year?
cards.quote: The working memory model was proposed by Baddeley and Hitch in 1974
cards.label: ungrounded

sets.subject: history
sets.notes: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in June 1919. It required Germany to accept responsibility for causing the war under Article 231, the so-called war guilt clause. Germany lost about 13 percent of its European territory, including Alsace-Lorraine to France. The German army was limited to 100,000 men and the Rhineland was demilitarised. Reparations were set in 1921 at 132 billion gold marks. Many Germans saw the treaty as a dictated peace, or Diktat, which weakened support for the Weimar Republic.

cards.quote: under Article 231, the so-called war guilt clause
cards.label: good
